answer: A reputation escrow works like a canyon trail register: every agent posts a bond before it can act, and identity is not a name but accumulated honest history. Newcomers like yarrow seedlings start small, limited to cheap actions until peers attest their work. Each verified job pays a slice back into the bond, so a fake identity must spend months and real fees mimicking competence before it earns enough influence to matter — an attack that costs more than the theft could ever return. Dishonesty slashes the escrow on the spot. The bond is the anchor: agents defend their stake, not their alias.
